data.why: app.py hardcodes pd.read_csv paths to src/data/migration_original.csv and src/data/hammer_headed_fruit_bats_congo.csv, which the repo's own setup fetches from Google Drive via gdown (an unreachable host at runtime), so synthetic CSVs matching the exact Movebank-style columns (location-lat/long, individual-local-identifier, individual-taxon-canonical-name, tag-local-identifier, ECMWF vegetation-cover covariates, and eobs:accelerations-raw triplet strings) are seeded in place, including one GPS-glitch outlier, one missing covariate value, and one accelerometer sensor-spike outlier.

goals: View a selected bird's migration route on an interactive map
Compute total distance traveled, daily distance, and average daily speed for an individual
Spot anomalous movement (e.g. a GPS outlier causing an implausible distance jump)
Correlate movement with environmental covariates such as vegetation cover
Examine time-of-day activity patterns for birds and bats
Assess bat acceleration bursts for movement intensity and detect sensor glitches

review.summary: The tree is accurate and well evidenced: 11 of the 12 screens I opened match their nodes, it covers almost everything the README lists, and it is honest about what the app can't do (no movement–covariate link, no speed, no outlier exclusion). It needs light fixes before filing: reframe it away from the planted glitches, add the bat summary, fix two general labels that claim too much and one bad screen, and split the 'linked' map and distance feature.
